database.config: default settings of the disposable service (shared_buffers etc. unchanged)
database.note: The PostgreSQL server runs in a container outside this process; its CPU and memory are not reported.

method: Each statement is run through EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) six times (first discarded) and the median execution time is reported, with migration 024 applied and again after dropping its three indexes (statistics re-analysed both times). Route timings are HTTP round trips to the real Express app over the same data. Events exist for selected runs only; adaptive runs carry no events in this data.

withMigration.note: Each probe runs in a transaction that is rolled back. Indexed columns defeat HOT updates, so the update figure is the worst case.

withoutMigration.note: Each probe runs in a transaction that is rolled back. Indexed columns defeat HOT updates, so the update figure is the worst case.

regressionsRouteSweep.reading: Doubling the runs roughly quadruples payload and time. The candidate index speeds the lookup by a modest factor but leaves the payload, which is the cost; the remedy is product code (bound or paginate replays per regression), not an index.

regressionsAtFullScale.statement: Repository#regressions() then JSON.stringify, as GET /api/regressions does (apps/api/src/app.ts:288)

knownLimits: Synthetic rows are uniform: 8 targets, 40 cases, 6 versions, one JSONB shape. Real data skew changes plans; re-run `npm run perf:plans` after a schema or query change.

Single run on one shared workstation; medians of five plan executions, not a statistical characterization. Compare ratios between the with and without columns, not absolute milliseconds across machines.
The disposable database is warm: blocks are served from PostgreSQL and OS caches, so disk latency is not represented.
Severity has no SQL predicate in the product, so there is no severity query to measure; see the migration header and tests/performance/migration-024.test.ts.
